Important: **The live-session guard only applies when resolving by session id** (the `else` branch). When the target is a `.jsonl` path (`target.endsWith('.jsonl')`), the presence check is **skipped entirely** — repairing a live session by path is allowed and will lose appends. That's a real inconsistency. Severity: IMPORTANT (data-loss risk on a documented path, but requires explicit path usage; still the guard exists and is bypassed). Given "when in doubt, start one level higher" and data loss is possible — could argue BLOCKING? The verdict rules: BLOCKING = correctness/bug/data loss. Repairing under a live writer loses data. But the by-path branch is arguably "advanced" usage. Hmm. The guard's own comment says "repairing under a writer loses appends" — and the by-id branch enforces it. The by-path branch silently skips it. I'd call this IMPORTANT (strong) or BLOCKING. Data loss is explicitly listed under BLOCKING. But is it a bug? Yes — inconsistent guard. I'll classify IMPORTANT-to-BLOCKING... Let me decide: the CLI resolves sessions two ways; one checks live, one doesn't. A user repairing "the file directly" would reasonably still be protected. The comment in the doc says "A session owned by a LIVE process (fresh presence heartbeat) is refused" — as a blanket statement, which is false for the path branch. I'll mark it BLOCKING? The machine: any BLOCKING → REQUEST_CHANGES. This is a genuine correctness issue in a data-loss direction. But it's also plausible the author intended path = expert mode. Still, the doc comment promises refusal. I lean IMPORTANT with a strong note, since the primary flow is guarded and path-based repair is an explicit escape hatch... but "repairing under a writer loses appends" applies equally. Data loss risk + doc mismatch → I'll go with BLOCKING. Hmm, let me weigh: review guidelines say "When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible." Risk: user runs `fa session repair <path>.jsonl` while session is live → appends lost silently. Not negligible. BLOCKING.

Also note: presenceStore is nullable (`presenceStore?.list()`), and by-id path — if presenceStore is null, no guard. Check how it's wired in cli_args/fah.dart.

Another point: after repair, presence/lock files? Also `.bak` collision: repeated repairs overwrite `.bak` — earlier backup lost. Suggestion.

Also in repairSessionLedgers: no `withSessionFileLock`. The open path uses withSessionFileLock. If repair runs while another `fa` process has the file open (not via presence), appends lost. The live guard mitigates. Also should check `renamePath` overwrite semantics — check the local FS implementation.

# Pull Request Information - **PR #**: 1247 - **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1247 - **Title**: gh-1073 Session JSONL grows unboundedly (12 GiB ledger records) → resume fails with 'Failed to read session' + heap-exhaustion crash - **Author**: ai-teammate - **Branch**: `ai/gh-1073` → `main` - **State**: open - **Files Changed**: 29 - **Additions**: +4680 - **Deletions**: -60 - **Created**: 2026-10-04T21:28:28Z - **Updated**: 2026-10-04T22:14:31Z ## PR Description ### What changed Bounded the session-JSONL growth that grew a month-long session to 12.4 GiB and made open/resume safe for huge files: ledger payloads are capped and deduped at the write site, the full open streams the file in bounded chunks (never one giant `String`) with a 2 GiB hard backstop, and a new `fa session repair` command rewrites bloated JSONLs. This leg fixed the last review leftovers: one analyzer lint and two stale retry-test assertions that still counted the old `readTextFile` open surface (the open now stats + streams, so the counters read `statCalls`). ### Key decisions - `ledger_caps.dart`: 300-char cap on every string field in `shell_job_registry` / `subagent_registry` records + `LedgerSnapshotDeduper` skips byte-identical snapshots at the write site - `model_request_summary`: per-message summaries capped (newest 64 messages / 256 KB budget); older messages degrade to role+chars stubs — record still describes the whole request - `JsonlSessionStorage._openLocked`: stat-first, refuse >2 GiB with a named `tooLarge` `SessionException` pointing at windowed resume / `fa session repair`; ranged filesystems get a fully streamed line-scan parse with header-only decode of giant `custom` ledgers (only the latest per `customType` is fully parsed — exactly what resume rehydration reads) - `session_repair.dart` + CLI: drop replay-only ledger types, keep-latest for snapshot registries, conservative (unknown/unparseable lines kept), backup + `--dry-run` ### How to verify ```bash dart test test/session test/trajectory test/task test/cli ``` Full core suite (`dart test --exclude-tags integration`): 7960 passed / 16 skipped. The 3 failures in `providers_queue_editor_test.dart` are environmental — the CI shell leaks `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE`, which the editor correctly refuses to override (all 13 pass with the var unset). A pre-existing glibc heap-corruption abort in the PTY-harness teardown also reproduces on the base commit and is unrelated.
Architecture diagram ```mermaid flowchart TD OPEN[Session open] --> STAT[fileInfo stat] STAT -->|> 2 GiB| REFUSE[tooLarge SessionException] REFUSE --> HINT[windowed resume / fa session repair] STAT -->|<= 2 GiB| STREAM[streamed line scan
bounded chunks] STREAM --> HDR[header-only decode
of giant custom ledgers] HDR --> LATEST[fully parse latest
record per customType] WRITE[ledger writes] --> CAP[ledger_caps: 300-char field cap] CAP --> DEDUP[skip identical snapshots] REPAIR[fa session repair] --> REWRITE[drop replay-only ledgers
keep-latest registries + backup] ```

4. In `_scanSegmentStreamed`, giant custom detection: `entry.data == null && rawLine.length >= threshold && rawLine.startsWith('{"type":"custom"')`. OK.

5. Potential bug: `latestGiantCustoms` map is keyed by customType but the rehydration loop at the end fully parses `rawLine` and replaces entry by id — good. But note: the map only holds the LATEST across segments because later writes overwrite — since segments scanned oldest-first, later segments win. But within a segment, later lines overwrite earlier — latest wins. Good. However if the same customType appears in a later segment but is NOT giant there (small record, data != null), the older giant rawLine remains in the map and gets fully parsed and replaces... wait, the small record in the later segment would have been added to entries with data != null and seenRecordIds.add. Then the older giant rawLine's full parse would replace... no — the full parse replaces the entry with `entries[indexWhere(e.id == full.id)]` — the giant record's id, which would be the entry in entries from the older segment (first copy wins dedupe). Hmm, but if a newer SMALL record of same type exists in a later segment, the stale giant from earlier segment would still be rehydrated and take precedence in the entries list, while resume rehydration reads "the latest per customType" from entries — which would then be the old giant rather than the new small record. Edge case; probably fine because dedupe and ordering mean the latest record of that type should be the last entry in entries with that customType. Actually rehydration reads latest entry per customType from entries — if old giant entry appears later in the list? No, older segment entries come first. So the latest entry with that customType would be the new small one. OK.

7. Blank line handling: blank lines are skipped but NOT added to goodSpans... they also aren't in tornSpans. So if a file has blank lines and a torn line triggers rewrite, the blank lines get dropped on rewrite. Fine.

But wait — there's a subtle bug: blank lines skipped means their spans are excluded from both good and torn spans; the rewrite copies only goodSpans, so blank lines disappear. OK, fine.

# Pull Request Information - **PR #**: 1247 - **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1247 - **Title**: gh-1073 Session JSONL grows unboundedly (12 GiB ledger records) → resume fails with 'Failed to read session' + heap-exhaustion crash - **Author**: ai-teammate - **Branch**: `ai/gh-1073` → `main` - **State**: open - **Files Changed**: 29 - **Additions**: +4680 - **Deletions**: -60 - **Created**: 2026-10-04T21:28:28Z - **Updated**: 2026-10-04T22:14:31Z ## PR Description ### What changed Bounded the session-JSONL growth that grew a month-long session to 12.4 GiB and made open/resume safe for huge files: ledger payloads are capped and deduped at the write site, the full open streams the file in bounded chunks (never one giant `String`) with a 2 GiB hard backstop, and a new `fa session repair` command rewrites bloated JSONLs. This leg fixed the last review leftovers: one analyzer lint and two stale retry-test assertions that still counted the old `readTextFile` open surface (the open now stats + streams, so the counters read `statCalls`). ### Key decisions - `ledger_caps.dart`: 300-char cap on every string field in `shell_job_registry` / `subagent_registry` records + `LedgerSnapshotDeduper` skips byte-identical snapshots at the write site - `model_request_summary`: per-message summaries capped (newest 64 messages / 256 KB budget); older messages degrade to role+chars stubs — record still describes the whole request - `JsonlSessionStorage._openLocked`: stat-first, refuse >2 GiB with a named `tooLarge` `SessionException` pointing at windowed resume / `fa session repair`; ranged filesystems get a fully streamed line-scan parse with header-only decode of giant `custom` ledgers (only the latest per `customType` is fully parsed — exactly what resume rehydration reads) - `session_repair.dart` + CLI: drop replay-only ledger types, keep-latest for snapshot registries, conservative (unknown/unparseable lines kept), backup + `--dry-run` ### How to verify ```bash dart test test/session test/trajectory test/task test/cli ``` Full core suite (`dart test --exclude-tags integration`): 7960 passed / 16 skipped. The 3 failures in `providers_queue_editor_test.dart` are environmental — the CI shell leaks `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE`, which the editor correctly refuses to override (all 13 pass with the var unset). A pre-existing glibc heap-corruption abort in the PTY-harness teardown also reproduces on the base commit and is unrelated.
Architecture diagram ```mermaid flowchart TD OPEN[Session open] --> STAT[fileInfo stat] STAT -->|> 2 GiB| REFUSE[tooLarge SessionException] REFUSE --> HINT[windowed resume / fa session repair] STAT -->|<= 2 GiB| STREAM[streamed line scan
bounded chunks] STREAM --> HDR[header-only decode
of giant custom ledgers] HDR --> LATEST[fully parse latest
record per customType] WRITE[ledger writes] --> CAP[ledger_caps: 300-char field cap] CAP --> DEDUP[skip identical snapshots] REPAIR[fa session repair] --> REWRITE[drop replay-only ledgers
keep-latest registries + backup] ```

But note: the map only holds the LATEST across segments because later writes overwrite — since segments scanned oldest-first, later segments win. But within a segment, later lines overwrite earlier — latest wins. Good. However if the same customType appears in a later segment but is NOT giant there (small record, data != null), the older giant rawLine remains in the map and gets fully parsed and replaces... wait, the small record in the later segment would have been added to entries with data != null and seenRecordIds.add. Edge case; probably fine because dedupe and ordering mean the latest record of that type should be the last entry in entries with that customType. Issues in session_repair.dart:

1. **CRITICAL BUG**: `_appendSpan` is defined at the bottom of `session_repair.dart` as a top-level private function, but it's ALSO defined in session_storage.dart. Duplicate code — but also wait: keptLatestCounts logic: for keep-latest types, on first occurrence `keptLatestCounts[customType] = 1` (only once per type — fine since only one kept per type). OK.

2. **Rollback bug**: if the swap `renamePath(tempPath, path)` fails, the code rolls the backup back: `await renamable.renamePath(backupPath, path)`. But the temp file `$path.repairing` is left behind — leak, minor.

3. **Bigger issue**: after successful repair, if a `.bak` already exists from a previous repair, `renamePath(path, backupPath)` — does rename overwrite? Depends on the FS implementation. If it fails because backup exists, repair fails. Check the local fs renamePath behavior. Possibly overwrites on POSIX (rename(2) replaces). OK.

4. **`keptLatestCounts`**: sets to 1 on first, then if more occurrences dropped... `latestByType` updated each time. Good.

If a running session appends while repair rewrites, the appended records after pass-1 scan are lost (rewrite overwrites with the temp file built from the pre-scan spans). # Pull Request Information - **PR #**: 1247 - **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1247 - **Title**: gh-1073 Session JSONL grows unboundedly (12 GiB ledger records) → resume fails with 'Failed to read session' + heap-exhaustion crash - **Author**: ai-teammate - **Branch**: `ai/gh-1073` → `main` - **State**: open - **Files Changed**: 29 - **Additions**: +4680 - **Deletions**: -60 - **Created**: 2026-10-04T21:28:28Z - **Updated**: 2026-10-04T22:14:31Z ## PR Description ### What changed Bounded the session-JSONL growth that grew a month-long session to 12.4 GiB and made open/resume safe for huge files: ledger payloads are capped and deduped at the write site, the full open streams the file in bounded chunks (never one giant `String`) with a 2 GiB hard backstop, and a new `fa session repair` command rewrites bloated JSONLs. This leg fixed the last review leftovers: one analyzer lint and two stale retry-test assertions that still counted the old `readTextFile` open surface (the open now stats + streams, so the counters read `statCalls`). ### Key decisions - `ledger_caps.dart`: 300-char cap on every string field in `shell_job_registry` / `subagent_registry` records + `LedgerSnapshotDeduper` skips byte-identical snapshots at the write site - `model_request_summary`: per-message summaries capped (newest 64 messages / 256 KB budget); older messages degrade to role+chars stubs — record still describes the whole request - `JsonlSessionStorage._openLocked`: stat-first, refuse >2 GiB with a named `tooLarge` `SessionException` pointing at windowed resume / `fa session repair`; ranged filesystems get a fully streamed line-scan parse with header-only decode of giant `custom` ledgers (only the latest per `customType` is fully parsed — exactly what resume rehydration reads) - `session_repair.dart` + CLI: drop replay-only ledger types, keep-latest for snapshot registries, conservative (unknown/unparseable lines kept), backup + `--dry-run` ### How to verify ```bash dart test test/session test/trajectory test/task test/cli ``` Full core suite (`dart test --exclude-tags integration`): 7960 passed / 16 skipped. The 3 failures in `providers_queue_editor_test.dart` are environmental — the CI shell leaks `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE`, which the editor correctly refuses to override (all 13 pass with the var unset). A pre-existing glibc heap-corruption abort in the PTY-harness teardown also reproduces on the base commit and is unrelated.
Architecture diagram ```mermaid flowchart TD OPEN[Session open] --> STAT[fileInfo stat] STAT -->|> 2 GiB| REFUSE[tooLarge SessionException] REFUSE --> HINT[windowed resume / fa session repair] STAT -->|<= 2 GiB| STREAM[streamed line scan
bounded chunks] STREAM --> HDR[header-only decode
of giant custom ledgers] HDR --> LATEST[fully parse latest
record per customType] WRITE[ledger writes] --> CAP[ledger_caps: 300-char field cap] CAP --> DEDUP[skip identical snapshots] REPAIR[fa session repair] --> REWRITE[drop replay-only ledgers
keep-latest registries + backup] ```

Interesting details:

1. In `_scanSegmentStreamed`, the quarantine appends `$text\n` to `.corrupt` sidecar — appends a newline after the raw line (raw line includes trailing newline already since span end includes the trailing `\n`). `utf8.decode(raw)` includes the `\n`, then appending `$text\n` adds an extra blank line per entry. Minor.

2. In the rewrite path: `wrote = await fs.writeFile(tempPath, '')` — writeFile signature returns Result? `var wrote` — ok.

3. The `rawLine.length >= shallowCustomRecordThreshold` — rawLine.length is UTF-16 code units of decoded text, while threshold presumably in bytes. Minor mismatch; check parseShallowCustomRecord in session_record or session_parse_executor.

4. In `_scanSegmentStreamed`, giant custom detection: `entry.data == null && rawLine.length >= threshold && rawLine.startsWith('{"type":"custom"')`. OK.

5. Potential bug: `latestGiantCustoms` map is keyed by customType but the rehydration loop at the end fully parses `rawLine` and replaces entry by id — good. But note: the map only holds the LATEST across segments because later writes overwrite — since segments scanned oldest-first, later segments win. But within a segment, later lines overwrite earlier — latest wins. Good. However if the same customType appears in a later segment but is NOT giant there (small record, data != null), the older giant rawLine remains in the map and gets fully parsed and replaces... wait, the small record in the later segment would have been added to entries with data != null and seenRecordIds.add. Then the older giant rawLine's full parse would replace... no — the full parse replaces the entry with `entries[indexWhere(e.id == full.id)]` — the giant record's id, which would be the entry in entries from the older segment (first copy wins dedupe). Hmm, but if a newer SMALL record of same type exists in a later segment, the stale giant from earlier segment would still be rehydrated and take precedence in the entries list, while resume rehydration reads "the latest per customType" from entries — which would then be the old giant rather than the new small record. Edge case; probably fine because dedupe and ordering mean the latest record of that type should be the last entry in entries with that customType. Actually rehydration reads latest entry per customType from entries — if old giant entry appears later in the list? No, older segment entries come first. So the latest entry with that customType would be the new small one. OK.

6. The timing var `parseMs` accumulation... `phaseSw` used for both readMs and rewriteMs — `rewriteMs = phaseSw.elapsedMilliseconds` measures since start of scan, not rewrite duration. Cosmetic.

7. Blank line handling: blank lines are skipped but NOT added to goodSpans... they also aren't in tornSpans. So if a file has blank lines and a torn line triggers rewrite, the blank lines get dropped on rewrite. Fine.

But wait — there's a subtle bug: blank lines skipped means their spans are excluded from both good and torn spans; the rewrite copies only goodSpans, so blank lines disappear. OK, fine.

8. `header ??= load.header;` — fall back to first segment's header if primary has none. Fine.

Now let me look at the remaining part of the session_storage diff (shallow parsing functions, parseShallowCustomRecord, sessionParseBatchMaxLines etc.) and also the rest of diff (later part). Then session_repair.dart, session_repair_command.dart, trajectory_record.dart, subagent_manager.dart, agent_loop.dart, cli files, and the huge bin/fah.dart change.

Observations so far:

1. In `agent_hub_cli.dart` `_persistJobBoard`: `final json = jsonEncode(_jobBoard.toRecords()); if (!_jobBoardPersistDeduper.shouldPersist(json)) return; await session.appendCustomEntry(..., data: _jobBoard.toRecords());` — encodes twice (once for dedupe, once inside appendCustomEntry presumably). Minor inefficiency/suggestion. Also a race: dedupe decision happens inside `_persistChain.then` — good, serialized with the chain. But note the deduper's `_lastJson` updates even if the append FAILS (catch swallows... actually the error handler comment says one failed append must not poison the chain). If append fails, deduper state says "persisted" and next identical snapshot gets skipped — snapshot lost until next mutation. Minor.

2. `_persistJobBoard` in subagent_manager: `_persist()` computes the snapshot synchronously outside the chain (`final snapshot = [...]`), so concurrent mutations could write stale snapshots out of order — but that's pre-existing behavior (the diff didn't change that part; snapshot computation was already outside). Actually pre-existing.

3. In `subagent_manager.dart` `_cappedRegistryRow`: `row['task'] as String?` — if `task` is not a String (e.g., int), the cast throws. `toJson()` presumably always produces a string. Also `?? ''` when null — fine.

4. `capTrajectoryRequestDetail`: creates stub `TrajectoryRequestMessageSummary(role:, chars:, preview: '')` — need to check constructor signature to confirm named params exist. Check trajectory_record.dart.

5. In `session_storage._scanSegmentStreamed`: The header parse — `parseSessionHeaderLine` on line 1 — if header invalid, throws? Also quarantine appends `$text\n` where text already includes trailing `\n` — double newline. Minor.

{"path":"lib/src/session_repair.dart"}

Issues in session_repair.dart:

1. **CRITICAL BUG**: `_appendSpan` is defined at the bottom of `session_repair.dart` as a top-level private function, but it's ALSO defined in session_storage.dart. Duplicate code — but also wait: keptLatestCounts logic: for keep-latest types, on first occurrence `keptLatestCounts[customType] = 1` (only once per type — fine since only one kept per type). OK.

2. **Rollback bug**: if the swap `renamePath(tempPath, path)` fails, the code rolls the backup back: `await renamable.renamePath(backupPath, path)`. But the temp file `$path.repairing` is left behind — leak, minor.

3. **Bigger issue**: after successful repair, if a `.bak` already exists from a previous repair, `renamePath(path, backupPath)` — does rename overwrite? Depends on the FS implementation. If it fails because backup exists, repair fails. Check the local fs renamePath behavior. Possibly overwrites on POSIX (rename(2) replaces). OK.

4. **`keptLatestCounts`**: sets to 1 on first, then if more occurrences dropped... `latestByType` updated each time. Good.

5. **Encoding issue**: `utf8.decode(raw, allowMalformed: true)` then `fs.appendFile(tempPath, text)` — appendFile presumably encodes UTF-8. Round-trip for valid lines is byte-exact. But for lines with malformed UTF-8 (torn), U+FFFD replacement changes bytes — acceptable, documented.

6. **Race/crash window**: rename original to .bak, then rename temp into place. If the process crashes between, the session file is missing (only .bak and .repairing). Window is small but the doc says "atomically" — it's not atomic as a whole. Worth a note, maybe suggestion.

7. **Missing file lock**: `repairSessionLedgers` doesn't take the session file lock (`withSessionFileLock`), while the open path locks. If a running session appends while repair rewrites, the appended records after pass-1 scan are lost (rewrite overwrites with the temp file built from the pre-scan spans). This is a real data-loss risk: repairing a session while `fa` is running against it drops records written between the scan and the swap. Should check whether CLI checks for live session. Check session_repair_command.dart.

8. Dry-run report `bytesAfter: bytesBefore` — but doesn't compute the after size; fine for dry run, though it'd be nice. It says `bytesBefore` when dryRun — documented.

Also note duplicated `_appendSpan` and `_formatBytes`-like helpers across files (session_storage has `_appendSpan` private too — private so no clash, but duplication).

Important: **The live-session guard only applies when resolving by session id** (the `else` branch). When the target is a `.jsonl` path (`target.endsWith('.jsonl')`), the presence check is **skipped entirely** — repairing a live session by path is allowed and will lose appends. That's a real inconsistency. Severity: IMPORTANT (data-loss risk on a documented path, but requires explicit path usage; still the guard exists and is bypassed). Given "when in doubt, start one level higher" and data loss is possible — could argue BLOCKING? The verdict rules: BLOCKING = correctness/bug/data loss. Repairing under a live writer loses data. But the by-path branch is arguably "advanced" usage. Hmm. The guard's own comment says "repairing under a writer loses appends" — and the by-id branch enforces it. The by-path branch silently skips it. I'd call this IMPORTANT (strong) or BLOCKING. Data loss is explicitly listed under BLOCKING. But is it a bug? Yes — inconsistent guard. I'll classify IMPORTANT-to-BLOCKING... Let me decide: the CLI resolves sessions two ways; one checks live, one doesn't. A user repairing "the file directly" would reasonably still be protected. The comment in the doc says "A session owned by a LIVE process (fresh presence heartbeat) is refused" — as a blanket statement, which is false for the path branch. I'll mark it BLOCKING? The machine: any BLOCKING → REQUEST_CHANGES. This is a genuine correctness issue in a data-loss direction. But it's also plausible the author intended path = expert mode. Still, the doc comment promises refusal. I lean IMPORTANT with a strong note, since the primary flow is guarded and path-based repair is an explicit escape hatch... but "repairing under a writer loses appends" applies equally. Data loss risk + doc mismatch → I'll go with BLOCKING. Hmm, let me weigh: review guidelines say "When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible." Risk: user runs `fa session repair <path>.jsonl` while session is live → appends lost silently. Not negligible. BLOCKING.

Also note: presenceStore is nullable (`presenceStore?.list()`), and by-id path — if presenceStore is null, no guard. Check how it's wired in cli_args/fah.dart.

Another point: after repair, presence/lock files? Also `.bak` collision: repeated repairs overwrite `.bak` — earlier backup lost. Suggestion.

Also in repairSessionLedgers: no `withSessionFileLock`. The open path uses withSessionFileLock. If repair runs while another `fa` process has the file open (not via presence), appends lost. The live guard mitigates. Also should check `renamePath` overwrite semantics — check the local FS implementation.

# Pull Request Information - **PR #**: 1247 - **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1247 - **Title**: gh-1073 Session JSONL grows unboundedly (12 GiB ledger records) → resume fails with 'Failed to read session' + heap-exhaustion crash - **Author**: ai-teammate - **Branch**: `ai/gh-1073` → `main` - **State**: open - **Files Changed**: 29 - **Additions**: +4680 - **Deletions**: -60 - **Created**: 2026-10-04T21:28:28Z - **Updated**: 2026-10-04T22:14:31Z ## PR Description ### What changed Bounded the session-JSONL growth that grew a month-long session to 12.4 GiB and made open/resume safe for huge files: ledger payloads are capped and deduped at the write site, the full open streams the file in bounded chunks (never one giant `String`) with a 2 GiB hard backstop, and a new `fa session repair` command rewrites bloated JSONLs. This leg fixed the last review leftovers: one analyzer lint and two stale retry-test assertions that still counted the old `readTextFile` open surface (the open now stats + streams, so the counters read `statCalls`). ### Key decisions - `ledger_caps.dart`: 300-char cap on every string field in `shell_job_registry` / `subagent_registry` records + `LedgerSnapshotDeduper` skips byte-identical snapshots at the write site - `model_request_summary`: per-message summaries capped (newest 64 messages / 256 KB budget); older messages degrade to role+chars stubs — record still describes the whole request - `JsonlSessionStorage._openLocked`: stat-first, refuse >2 GiB with a named `tooLarge` `SessionException` pointing at windowed resume / `fa session repair`; ranged filesystems get a fully streamed line-scan parse with header-only decode of giant `custom` ledgers (only the latest per `customType` is fully parsed — exactly what resume rehydration reads) - `session_repair.dart` + CLI: drop replay-only ledger types, keep-latest for snapshot registries, conservative (unknown/unparseable lines kept), backup + `--dry-run` ### How to verify ```bash dart test test/session test/trajectory test/task test/cli ``` Full core suite (`dart test --exclude-tags integration`): 7960 passed / 16 skipped. The 3 failures in `providers_queue_editor_test.dart` are environmental — the CI shell leaks `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE`, which the editor correctly refuses to override (all 13 pass with the var unset). A pre-existing glibc heap-corruption abort in the PTY-harness teardown also reproduces on the base commit and is unrelated.

keep-latest registries + backup] ```

In `_scanSegmentStreamed`, the quarantine appends `$text\n` to `.corrupt` sidecar — appends a newline after the raw line (raw line includes trailing newline already since span end includes the trailing `\n`). `utf8.decode(raw)` includes the `\n`, then appending `$text\n` adds an extra blank line per entry. 2. In the rewrite path: `wrote = await fs.writeFile(tempPath, '')` — writeFile signature returns Result? `var wrote` — ok.

3. The `rawLine.length >= shallowCustomRecordThreshold` — rawLine.length is UTF-16 code units of decoded text, while threshold presumably in bytes. Minor mismatch; check parseShallowCustomRecord in session_record or session_parse_executor.

4. In `_scanSegmentStreamed`, giant custom detection: `entry.data == null && rawLine.length >= threshold && rawLine.startsWith('{"type":"custom"')`. OK.

5. Potential bug: `latestGiantCustoms` map is keyed by customType but the rehydration loop at the end fully parses `rawLine` and replaces entry by id — good. But note: the map only holds the LATEST across segments because later writes overwrite — since segments scanned oldest-first, later segments win. But within a segment, later lines overwrite earlier — latest wins. Good. However if the same customType appears in a later segment but is NOT giant there (small record, data != null), the older giant rawLine remains in the map and gets fully parsed and replaces... wait, the small record in the later segment would have been added to entries with data != null and seenRecordIds.add. Then the older giant rawLine's full parse would replace... no — the full parse replaces the entry with `entries[indexWhere(e.id == full.id)]` — the giant record's id, which would be the entry in entries from the older segment (first copy wins dedupe). Hmm, but if a newer SMALL record of same type exists in a later segment, the stale giant from earlier segment would still be rehydrated and take precedence in the entries list, while resume rehydration reads "the latest per customType" from entries — which would then be the old giant rather than the new small record. Edge case; probably fine because dedupe and ordering mean the latest record of that type should be the last entry in entries with that customType. # Pull Request Information - **PR #**: 1247 - **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1247 - **Title**: gh-1073 Session JSONL grows unboundedly (12 GiB ledger records) → resume fails with 'Failed to read session' + heap-exhaustion crash - **Author**: ai-teammate - **Branch**: `ai/gh-1073` → `main` - **State**: open - **Files Changed**: 29 - **Additions**: +4680 - **Deletions**: -60 - **Created**: 2026-10-04T21:28:28Z - **Updated**: 2026-10-04T22:14:31Z ## PR Description ### What changed Bounded the session-JSONL growth that grew a month-long session to 12.4 GiB and made open/resume safe for huge files: ledger payloads are capped and deduped at the write site, the full open streams the file in bounded chunks (never one giant `String`) with a 2 GiB hard backstop, and a new `fa session repair` command rewrites bloated JSONLs. This leg fixed the last review leftovers: one analyzer lint and two stale retry-test assertions that still counted the old `readTextFile` open surface (the open now stats + streams, so the counters read `statCalls`). ### Key decisions - `ledger_caps.dart`: 300-char cap on every string field in `shell_job_registry` / `subagent_registry` records + `LedgerSnapshotDeduper` skips byte-identical snapshots at the write site - `model_request_summary`: per-message summaries capped (newest 64 messages / 256 KB budget); older messages degrade to role+chars stubs — record still describes the whole request - `JsonlSessionStorage._openLocked`: stat-first, refuse >2 GiB with a named `tooLarge` `SessionException` pointing at windowed resume / `fa session repair`; ranged filesystems get a fully streamed line-scan parse with header-only decode of giant `custom` ledgers (only the latest per `customType` is fully parsed — exactly what resume rehydration reads) - `session_repair.dart` + CLI: drop replay-only ledger types, keep-latest for snapshot registries, conservative (unknown/unparseable lines kept), backup + `--dry-run` ### How to verify ```bash dart test test/session test/trajectory test/task test/cli ``` Full core suite (`dart test --exclude-tags integration`): 7960 passed / 16 skipped. The 3 failures in `providers_queue_editor_test.dart` are environmental — the CI shell leaks `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE`, which the editor correctly refuses to override (all 13 pass with the var unset). A pre-existing glibc heap-corruption abort in the PTY-harness teardown also reproduces on the base commit and is unrelated.

bounded chunks] STREAM --> HDR[header-only decode
of giant custom ledgers] HDR --> LATEST[fully parse latest
record per customType] WRITE[ledger writes] --> CAP[ledger_caps: 300-char field cap] CAP --> DEDUP[skip identical snapshots] REPAIR[fa session repair] --> REWRITE[drop replay-only ledgers
keep-latest registries + backup] ```

In `_scanSegmentStreamed`, the quarantine appends `$text\n` to `.corrupt` sidecar — appends a newline after the raw line (raw line includes trailing newline already since span end includes the trailing `\n`). `utf8.decode(raw)` includes the `\n`, then appending `$text\n` adds an extra blank line per entry. Minor.

2. In the rewrite path: `wrote = await fs.writeFile(tempPath, '')` — writeFile signature returns Result? `var wrote` — ok.

3. The `rawLine.length >= shallowCustomRecordThreshold` — rawLine.length is UTF-16 code units of decoded text, while threshold presumably in bytes. Minor mismatch; check parseShallowCustomRecord in session_record or session_parse_executor.

4. In `_scanSegmentStreamed`, giant custom detection: `entry.data == null && rawLine.length >= threshold && rawLine.startsWith('{"type":"custom"')`. OK.

5. Potential bug: `latestGiantCustoms` map is keyed by customType but the rehydration loop at the end fully parses `rawLine` and replaces entry by id — good. But note: the map only holds the LATEST across segments because later writes overwrite — since segments scanned oldest-first, later segments win. But within a segment, later lines overwrite earlier — latest wins. Good. However if the same customType appears in a later segment but is NOT giant there (small record, data != null), the older giant rawLine remains in the map and gets fully parsed and replaces... wait, the small record in the later segment would have been added to entries with data != null and seenRecordIds.add. Then the older giant rawLine's full parse would replace... no — the full parse replaces the entry with `entries[indexWhere(e.id == full.id)]` — the giant record's id, which would be the entry in entries from the older segment (first copy wins dedupe). Hmm, but if a newer SMALL record of same type exists in a later segment, the stale giant from earlier segment would still be rehydrated and take precedence in the entries list, while resume rehydration reads "the latest per customType" from entries — which would then be the old giant rather than the new small record. Edge case; probably fine because dedupe and ordering mean the latest record of that type should be the last entry in entries with that customType. Actually rehydration reads latest entry per customType from entries — if old giant entry appears later in the list? No, older segment entries come first. So the latest entry with that customType would be the new small one. OK.

6. The timing var `parseMs` accumulation... `phaseSw` used for both readMs and rewriteMs — `rewriteMs = phaseSw.elapsedMilliseconds` measures since start of scan, not rewrite duration. Cosmetic.

7. Blank line handling: blank lines are skipped but NOT added to goodSpans... they also aren't in tornSpans. So if a file has blank lines and a torn line triggers rewrite, the blank lines get dropped on rewrite. Fine.

But wait — there's a subtle bug: blank lines skipped means their spans are excluded from both good and torn spans; the rewrite copies only goodSpans, so blank lines disappear. OK, fine.

# Pull Request Information - **PR #**: 1247 - **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1247 - **Title**: gh-1073 Session JSONL grows unboundedly (12 GiB ledger records) → resume fails with 'Failed to read session' + heap-exhaustion crash - **Author**: ai-teammate - **Branch**: `ai/gh-1073` → `main` - **State**: open - **Files Changed**: 29 - **Additions**: +4680 - **Deletions**: -60 - **Created**: 2026-10-04T21:28:28Z - **Updated**: 2026-10-04T22:14:31Z ## PR Description ### What changed Bounded the session-JSONL growth that grew a month-long session to 12.4 GiB and made open/resume safe for huge files: ledger payloads are capped and deduped at the write site, the full open streams the file in bounded chunks (never one giant `String`) with a 2 GiB hard backstop, and a new `fa session repair` command rewrites bloated JSONLs. This leg fixed the last review leftovers: one analyzer lint and two stale retry-test assertions that still counted the old `readTextFile` open surface (the open now stats + streams, so the counters read `statCalls`). ### Key decisions - `ledger_caps.dart`: 300-char cap on every string field in `shell_job_registry` / `subagent_registry` records + `LedgerSnapshotDeduper` skips byte-identical snapshots at the write site - `model_request_summary`: per-message summaries capped (newest 64 messages / 256 KB budget); older messages degrade to role+chars stubs — record still describes the whole request - `JsonlSessionStorage._openLocked`: stat-first, refuse >2 GiB with a named `tooLarge` `SessionException` pointing at windowed resume / `fa session repair`; ranged filesystems get a fully streamed line-scan parse with header-only decode of giant `custom` ledgers (only the latest per `customType` is fully parsed — exactly what resume rehydration reads) - `session_repair.dart` + CLI: drop replay-only ledger types, keep-latest for snapshot registries, conservative (unknown/unparseable lines kept), backup + `--dry-run` ### How to verify ```bash dart test test/session test/trajectory test/task test/cli ``` Full core suite (`dart test --exclude-tags integration`): 7960 passed / 16 skipped. The 3 failures in `providers_queue_editor_test.dart` are environmental — the CI shell leaks `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE`, which the editor correctly refuses to override (all 13 pass with the var unset). A pre-existing glibc heap-corruption abort in the PTY-harness teardown also reproduces on the base commit and is unrelated.
Architecture diagram ```mermaid flowchart TD OPEN[Session open] --> STAT[fileInfo stat] STAT -->|> 2 GiB| REFUSE[tooLarge SessionException] REFUSE --> HINT[windowed resume / fa session repair] STAT -->|<= 2 GiB| STREAM[streamed line scan
bounded chunks] STREAM --> HDR[header-only decode
of giant custom ledgers] HDR --> LATEST[fully parse latest
record per customType] WRITE[ledger writes] --> CAP[ledger_caps: 300-char field cap] CAP --> DEDUP[skip identical snapshots] REPAIR[fa session repair] --> REWRITE[drop replay-only ledgers
keep-latest registries + backup] ```

# Pull Request Information - **PR #**: 1247 - **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1247 - **Title**: gh-1073 Session JSONL grows unboundedly (12 GiB ledger records) → resume fails with 'Failed to read session' + heap-exhaustion crash - **Author**: ai-teammate - **Branch**: `ai/gh-1073` → `main` - **State**: open - **Files Changed**: 29 - **Additions**: +4680 - **Deletions**: -60 - **Created**: 2026-10-04T21:28:28Z - **Updated**: 2026-10-04T22:14:31Z ## PR Description ### What changed Bounded the session-JSONL growth that grew a month-long session to 12.4 GiB and made open/resume safe for huge files: ledger payloads are capped and deduped at the write site, the full open streams the file in bounded chunks (never one giant `String`) with a 2 GiB hard backstop, and a new `fa session repair` command rewrites bloated JSONLs. This leg fixed the last review leftovers: one analyzer lint and two stale retry-test assertions that still counted the old `readTextFile` open surface (the open now stats + streams, so the counters read `statCalls`). ### Key decisions - `ledger_caps.dart`: 300-char cap on every string field in `shell_job_registry` / `subagent_registry` records + `LedgerSnapshotDeduper` skips byte-identical snapshots at the write site - `model_request_summary`: per-message summaries capped (newest 64 messages / 256 KB budget); older messages degrade to role+chars stubs — record still describes the whole request - `JsonlSessionStorage._openLocked`: stat-first, refuse >2 GiB with a named `tooLarge` `SessionException` pointing at windowed resume / `fa session repair`; ranged filesystems get a fully streamed line-scan parse with header-only decode of giant `custom` ledgers (only the latest per `customType` is fully parsed — exactly what resume rehydration reads) - `session_repair.dart` + CLI: drop replay-only ledger types, keep-latest for snapshot registries, conservative (unknown/unparseable lines kept), backup + `--dry-run` ### How to verify ```bash dart test test/session test/trajectory test/task test/cli ``` Full core suite (`dart test --exclude-tags integration`): 7960 passed / 16 skipped. The 3 failures in `providers_queue_editor_test.dart` are environmental — the CI shell leaks `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE`, which the editor correctly refuses to override (all 13 pass with the var unset). A pre-existing glibc heap-corruption abort in the PTY-harness teardown also reproduces on the base commit and is unrelated.
Architecture diagram ```mermaid flowchart TD OPEN[Session open] --> STAT[fileInfo stat] STAT -->|> 2 GiB| REFUSE[tooLarge SessionException] REFUSE --> HINT[windowed resume / fa session repair] STAT -->|<= 2 GiB| STREAM[streamed line scan
bounded chunks] STREAM --> HDR[header-only decode
of giant custom ledgers] HDR --> LATEST[fully parse latest
record per customType] WRITE[ledger writes] --> CAP[ledger_caps: 300-char field cap] CAP --> DEDUP[skip identical snapshots] REPAIR[fa session repair] --> REWRITE[drop replay-only ledgers
keep-latest registries + backup] ```

This leg fixed the last review leftovers: one analyzer lint and two stale retry-test assertions that still counted the old `readTextFile` open surface (the open now stats + streams, so the counters read `statCalls`). ### Key decisions - `ledger_caps.dart`: 300-char cap on every string field in `shell_job_registry` / `subagent_registry` records + `LedgerSnapshotDeduper` skips byte-identical snapshots at the write site - `model_request_summary`: per-message summaries capped (newest 64 messages / 256 KB budget); older messages degrade to role+chars stubs — record still describes the whole request - `JsonlSessionStorage._openLocked`: stat-first, refuse >2 GiB with a named `tooLarge` `SessionException` pointing at windowed resume / `fa session repair`; ranged filesystems get a fully streamed line-scan parse with header-only decode of giant `custom` ledgers (only the latest per `customType` is fully parsed — exactly what resume rehydration reads) - `session_repair.dart` + CLI: drop replay-only ledger types, keep-latest for snapshot registries, conservative (unknown/unparseable lines kept), backup + `--dry-run` ### How to verify ```bash dart test test/session test/trajectory test/task test/cli ``` Full core suite (`dart test --exclude-tags integration`): 7960 passed / 16 skipped. The 3 failures in `providers_queue_editor_test.dart` are environmental — the CI shell leaks `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE`, which the editor correctly refuses to override (all 13 pass with the var unset). A pre-existing glibc heap-corruption abort in the PTY-harness teardown also reproduces on the base commit and is unrelated.

keep-latest registries + backup] ```

One subtle bug candidate in `_scanSegmentStreamed`'s giant-custom detection:

```dart
if (entry is CustomRecord &&
    entry.data == null &&
    rawLine.length >= shallowCustomRecordThreshold &&
    rawLine.startsWith('{"type":"custom"')) {
  latestGiantCustoms[entry.customType] = rawLine;
}
```

`entry.data == null` also matches a genuine custom record with null data (not shallow-parsed, e.g. a small record... no, small records have data; but a custom record that legitimately has `data: null` and line < threshold won't match due to length check). But: a giant custom record where `shallowCustomHeader` returned null (foreign field order) gets fully parsed with real data → entry.data != null → not added to latestGiantCustoms. Fine.

But a real edge: a giant `custom` record with data==null that is NOT a ledger — e.g. some custom type where data is legitimately null. Then latestGiantCustoms[customType] = rawLine and at rehydration it's fully parsed with parseSessionEntryLine — result has data==null anyway. Fine.

Rehydration loop: `final full = parseSessionEntryLine(rawLine, filePath, 0);` — uses `filePath` (primary path) as filePath param even for records from part segments; error messages would name the wrong file. Cosmetic.

Also, the rehydration `entries.indexWhere((e) => e.id == full.id)` — O(n²) worst case per giant type. n = entries length, and indexWhere is O(n). With few ledger types, fine.

One more important check in `_scanSegmentStreamed`: `batchFirstLineNumber = 2` initial. Line 1 is the header. OK.

Blank lines: skipped, not counted in batchFirstLineNumber... batchFirstLineNumber increments only by batchLines.length (non-blank). Line numbers in error messages will drift from actual file lines when blank lines present. Pre-existing semantics likely similar in whole-file path? Minor.

pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. # Pull Request Information - **PR #**: 1247 - **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1247 - **Title**: gh-1073 Session JSONL grows unboundedly (12 GiB ledger records) → resume fails with 'Failed to read session' + heap-exhaustion crash - **Author**: ai-teammate - **Branch**: `ai/gh-1073` → `main` - **State**: open - **Files Changed**: 29 - **Additions**: +4680 - **Deletions**: -60 - **Created**: 2026-10-04T21:28:28Z - **Updated**: 2026-10-04T22:14:31Z ## PR Description ### What changed Bounded the session-JSONL growth that grew a month-long session to 12.4 GiB and made open/resume safe for huge files: ledger payloads are capped and deduped at the write site, the full open streams the file in bounded chunks (never one giant `String`) with a 2 GiB hard backstop, and a new `fa session repair` command rewrites bloated JSONLs. This leg fixed the last review leftovers: one analyzer lint and two stale retry-test assertions that still counted the old `readTextFile` open surface (the open now stats + streams, so the counters read `statCalls`). ### Key decisions - `ledger_caps.dart`: 300-char cap on every string field in `shell_job_registry` / `subagent_registry` records + `LedgerSnapshotDeduper` skips byte-identical snapshots at the write site - `model_request_summary`: per-message summaries capped (newest 64 messages / 256 KB budget); older messages degrade to role+chars stubs — record still describes the whole request - `JsonlSessionStorage._openLocked`: stat-first, refuse >2 GiB with a named `tooLarge` `SessionException` pointing at windowed resume / `fa session repair`; ranged filesystems get a fully streamed line-scan parse with header-only decode of giant `custom` ledgers (only the latest per `customType` is fully parsed — exactly what resume rehydration reads) - `session_repair.dart` + CLI: drop replay-only ledger types, keep-latest for snapshot registries, conservative (unknown/unparseable lines kept), backup + `--dry-run` ### How to verify ```bash dart test test/session test/trajectory test/task test/cli ``` Full core suite (`dart test --exclude-tags integration`): 7960 passed / 16 skipped. The 3 failures in `providers_queue_editor_test.dart` are environmental — the CI shell leaks `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE`, which the editor correctly refuses to override (all 13 pass with the var unset). A pre-existing glibc heap-corruption abort in the PTY-harness teardown also reproduces on the base commit and is unrelated.
Architecture diagram ```mermaid flowchart TD OPEN[Session open] --> STAT[fileInfo stat] STAT -->|> 2 GiB| REFUSE[tooLarge SessionException] REFUSE --> HINT[windowed resume / fa session repair] STAT -->|<= 2 GiB| STREAM[streamed line scan
bounded chunks] STREAM --> HDR[header-only decode
of giant custom ledgers] HDR --> LATEST[fully parse latest
record per customType] WRITE[ledger writes] --> CAP[ledger_caps: 300-char field cap] CAP --> DEDUP[skip identical snapshots] REPAIR[fa session repair] --> REWRITE[drop replay-only ledgers
keep-latest registries + backup] ```

# pr-1247: gh-1073 Session JSONL grows unboundedly (12 GiB ledger records) → resume fails with 'Failed to read session' + heap-exhaustion crash ## Description ### What changed Bounded the session-JSONL growth that grew a month-long session to 12.4 GiB and made open/resume safe for huge files: ledger payloads are capped and deduped at the write site, the full open streams the file in bounded chunks (never one giant `String`) with a 2 GiB hard backstop, and a new `fa session repair` command rewrites bloated JSONLs. This leg fixed the last review leftovers: one analyzer lint and two stale retry-test assertions that still counted the old `readTextFile` open surface (the open now stats + streams, so the counters read `statCalls`). ### Key decisions - `ledger_caps.dart`: 300-char cap on every string field in `shell_job_registry` / `subagent_registry` records + `LedgerSnapshotDeduper` skips byte-identical snapshots at the write site - `model_request_summary`: per-message summaries capped (newest 64 messages / 256 KB budget); older messages degrade to role+chars stubs — record still describes the whole request - `JsonlSessionStorage._openLocked`: stat-first, refuse >2 GiB with a named `tooLarge` `SessionException` pointing at windowed resume / `fa session repair`; ranged filesystems get a fully streamed line-scan parse with header-only decode of giant `custom` ledgers (only the latest per `customType` is fully parsed — exactly what resume rehydration reads) - `session_repair.dart` + CLI: drop replay-only ledger types, keep-latest for snapshot registries, conservative (unknown/unparseable lines kept), backup + `--dry-run` ### How to verify ```bash dart test test/session test/trajectory test/task test/cli ``` Full core suite (`dart test --exclude-tags integration`): 7960 passed / 16 skipped. The 3 failures in `providers_queue_editor_test.dart` are environmental — the CI shell leaks `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE`, which the editor correctly refuses to override (all 13 pass with the var unset). A pre-existing glibc heap-corruption abort in the PTY-harness teardown also reproduces on the base commit and is unrelated.
Architecture diagram ```mermaid flowchart TD OPEN[Session open] --> STAT[fileInfo stat] STAT -->|> 2 GiB| REFUSE[tooLarge SessionException] REFUSE --> HINT[windowed resume / fa session repair] STAT -->|<= 2 GiB| STREAM[streamed line scan
bounded chunks] STREAM --> HDR[header-only decode
of giant custom ledgers] HDR --> LATEST[fully parse latest
record per customType] WRITE[ledger writes] --> CAP[ledger_caps: 300-char field cap] CAP --> DEDUP[skip identical snapshots] REPAIR[fa session repair] --> REWRITE[drop replay-only ledgers
keep-latest registries + backup] ```

Confirmed the story: main's commit 48d1ffa1f (gh-1232, PR #1236) split bin/fah.dart into part files. This PR's branch (gh-1073, started 2026-09-29) had an old inlined fah.dart, and merging main in (a9ac5b40b "Merge branch 'main'") resolved the conflict by keeping the branch's old monolithic fah.dart, which:
- lost the `part` directives + imports for fah_boot_restore/fah_wire_serve/jsr_cli,
- left the part files orphaned (599 analyzer errors),
- silently dropped `fa wire-serve`, `fa jsr`, and the gh-1000 boot-restore pin,
- breaks test/bin_boot_restore_pin_test.dart.

`dart analyze bin/fah.dart` alone is clean, so the author likely ran targeted analysis and missed it. But CI runs `dart analyze` (full) and `dart analyze lib test bin` → red. Plus the failing pin test. This is clearly BLOCKING (multiple). The PR description doesn't mention any of this — it's an accidental merge artifact, massive scope damage rather than scope creep.

Let me quickly verify how many of the 661 issues are in which files, to write an accurate comment. Also verify `fa wire-serve` test coverage: test/integration/wire_serve_cli_test.dart imports bin/fah_wire_serve.dart (still exists, fine). Is there a test that runs the fah binary with wire-serve? Not needed.

Also check: does HEAD's fah.dart handle `serve --a2a/--bridge`? Yes (splitServeA2aArgs used at line 1167). OK.

Now let me also check remaining review areas:
- session_io_retry_test.dart, session_streamed_open_test.dart etc. (tests) — briefly.
- `shallowCustomHeader` and `parseShallowCustomRecord` in session parsing.
- Also `dbg_heal_test.dart` — 37 lines added; what's that? Check.
- The deduper's behavior in `_persistJobBoard`: jsonEncode computed but data re-encoded — minor perf. Also `_jobBoard.toRecords()` called twice.
- `ledgetTextCapChars` typo.
- session_repair by-path live guard skip (IMPORTANT/BLOCKING — data loss). Given the analyzer/CI breakage dominates, REQUEST_CHANGES regardless.

Let me look at the shallow parse helpers and the rest of the session_storage diff (the parts after line 461 were just the moved whole-file open). Check shallowCustomHeader/shallowCustomRecordThreshold definitions.
Now let me check the shallow-parse helpers and a few remaining pieces.
{"command":"grep -rn \"shallowCustomRecordThreshold\\|shallowCustomHeader\\|parseShallowCustomRecord\\|shallowGiantCustoms\" lib/src --include=\"*.dart\" | grep -v test | head -20"}
{"command":"sed -n 255,330p lib/src/session/session_storage.dart; echo ===; sed -n 195,240p lib/src/env/session_parse_executor.dart"}

One subtle bug candidate in `_scanSegmentStreamed`'s giant-custom detection:

```dart
if (entry is CustomRecord &&
    entry.data == null &&
    rawLine.length >= shallowCustomRecordThreshold &&
    rawLine.startsWith('{"type":"custom"')) {
  latestGiantCustoms[entry.customType] = rawLine;
}
```

`entry.data == null` also matches a genuine custom record with null data (not shallow-parsed, e.g. a small record... no, small records have data; but a custom record that legitimately has `data: null` and line < threshold won't match due to length check). But: a giant custom record where `shallowCustomHeader` returned null (foreign field order) gets fully parsed with real data → entry.data != null → not added to latestGiantCustoms. Fine.

But a real edge: a giant `custom` record with data==null that is NOT a ledger — e.g. some custom type where data is legitimately null. Then latestGiantCustoms[customType] = rawLine and at rehydration it's fully parsed with parseSessionEntryLine — result has data==null anyway. Fine.

Rehydration loop: `final full = parseSessionEntryLine(rawLine, filePath, 0);` — uses `filePath` (primary path) as filePath param even for records from part segments; error messages would name the wrong file. Cosmetic.

Also, the rehydration `entries.indexWhere((e) => e.id == full.id)` — O(n²) worst case per giant type. n = entries length, and indexWhere is O(n). With few ledger types, fine.

One more important check in `_scanSegmentStreamed`: `batchFirstLineNumber = 2` initial. Line 1 is the header. OK.

Blank lines: skipped, not counted in batchFirstLineNumber... batchFirstLineNumber increments only by batchLines.length (non-blank). Line numbers in error messages will drift from actual file lines when blank lines present. Pre-existing semantics likely similar in whole-file path? Minor.

Deduper subtlety in `_persistJobBoard` (agent_hub_cli.dart): the dedupe check runs INSIDE the chain, good. But `_jobBoard.toRecords()` is invoked twice (once for jsonEncode, once for data) — between them the board may mutate? No — inside the chain's then, synchronous up to the await. Actually `jsonEncode(_jobBoard.toRecords())` then `session.appendCustomEntry(... data: _jobBoard.toRecords())` — both synchronous calls before the await, no interleaving. Fine; just double serialization cost. Suggestion.

Bigger deduper issue: `_lastJson` updates before the write; if `appendCustomEntry` throws (caught by `.catchError`?), the deduper believes it persisted, so a later identical snapshot is skipped — the latest state never lands in the ledger until the next mutation. Window is small. Suggestion-level at most.

Now — the `session repair` live-guard bypass via `.jsonl` path branch. Also note in cli wiring, `presenceStore` is passed. In `runSessionRepairCliCommand`, presence check only in else branch. I'll classify this IMPORTANT (not blocking, since the dominant flow is guarded and the path form is an explicit advanced escape hatch — but the doc comment promises refusal for any live session). Hmm, "when in doubt, start one level higher". The function's doc says "A session owned by a LIVE process (fresh presence heartbeat) is refused" — that's a false claim for the path branch. Data loss = silent record loss. I could mark BLOCKING. But given the review already has multiple BLOCKINGs, classification accuracy matters. I'll go IMPORTANT with clear reasoning: by-id (the documented flow) is guarded; path mode is a deliberate expert escape hatch analogous to rm -f. Actually wait — is it deliberate? Nothing in the code suggests deliberateness; the guard comment lives inside the else branch. The help text says "A live session (fresh heartbeat) is refused" unconditionally. I'll keep IMPORTANT but strongly worded. Hmm, the instructions say data loss → BLOCKING. Repairing a live session by path DOES lose appends silently. I'll go BLOCKING? Let me think about likelihood: the exact scenario from gh-1073 is a 12 GiB session that fails to open — likely NOT live (the process crashed/OOMed). A user repairing by path is repairing precisely such dead files. The live-process risk for path mode requires an active `fa` running with an explicit path target. Real but narrow. IMPORTANT it is — strong wording.

Also `repairSessionLedgers` doesn't take the session file lock — concurrent opens/writes during the scan→swap window lose appends even for a non-"presence-live" but briefly-running process. Same theme.

Other findings:

1. `ledgetTextCapChars` typo (ledger) — SUGGESTION.
2. Duplicate `_appendSpan` in session_repair.dart and session_storage.dart — SUGGESTION (extract to shared util; private so no symbol clash).
3. Quarantine double newline: `await fs.appendFile('$segmentPath.corrupt', '$text\n')` where text already ends with `\n` (span includes trailing newline) → extra blank line per entry. SUGGESTION/IMPORTANT-minor.
4. `_formatBytes` duplicated in session_repair (`_bytes`) and session_storage — SUGGESTION.
5. In `_scanSegmentStreamed` rewrite: decode→appendFile as STRING; `fs.appendFile` presumably encodes UTF-8 — byte-exact for valid lines as documented. But wait: lines were decoded with allowMalformed; JSON-valid lines can't contain malformed UTF-8 in strings... a JSON string can contain raw bytes? No, JSON strings must be valid Unicode escapes or valid UTF-8. OK.
6. `sessionParseBatchMaxLines`/`sessionParseBatchMaxBytes` — check they exist. Presumably yes since compiled clean.
7. Timing: `rewriteMs = phaseSw.elapsedMilliseconds` — measures from scan start, mislabeled. SUGGESTION.
8. In `_openStreamedLocked`: `parseMs` only accumulates the rehydration phase; batch parsing time isn't captured (it's inside readMs via `_scanSegmentStreamed`'s readMs which includes flushBatch await). Timing-log cosmetic. SUGGESTION, low value — skip or bundle.
9. `bin/fah.dart` giant inline + dropped commands + orphaned parts + 599 analyze errors + failing pin test — BLOCKING (this is the big one; I'll write one comprehensive BLOCKING comment on the removed `part`/`import` lines in bin/fah.dart, which ARE in the diff).
10. `_persistJobBoard` double `toRecords()`/encode — SUGGESTION.
11. Deduper state advance before confirmed write — SUGGESTION.
12. `subagent_manager._cappedRegistryRow` cast `row['task'] as String?` — if task were missing, `?? ''` writes empty task... fine. What if row['task'] is not a String (e.g. num)? cast throws inside `_persist` → `_persist` is sync void called from mutation sites — a throw would propagate to caller. Check toJson always emits String task. Probably fine; skip.
13. `_openLocked`: for non-ranged FS, `_openWholeFileLocked` is used; but the stat+refuse happens first — good. But note `_openWholeFileLocked` for a 2 GiB file on a web FS materializes 2 GiB string... bound exists (2 GiB) so worst case is still huge. Acceptable by design.
14. Session repair: repeated repair overwrites `.bak` (previous backup lost silently). SUGGESTION.
15. Session repair crash window between the two renames leaves session missing (original at .bak, temp at .repairing). The swap+rollback handles rename failure but not process crash. SUGGESTION (documented "atomically" overclaims). Minor.
16. `keptLatestCounts[customType] = 1` — set inside else only; fine.
17. In repair, `_sniffCustomType` jsonDecode(header) on every custom line — header up to 64KB... fine.
18. Repair: `recordsKept = keptSpans.length` — includes merged spans? `_appendSpan` merges contiguous spans, so keptSpans.length ≤ kept lines. Report says "recordsKept" but counts spans, not records — after merging, keptSpans.length < actual records kept. Cosmetic inaccuracy in report. Also dryRun bytesAfter = bytesBefore — by design.

Also `capTrajectoryRequestDetail`: the stub uses `chars: messages[i].chars` — check TrajectoryRequestMessageSummary constructor signature has `chars` and `preview` named params and `role`. Compiled clean so fine.

One more check — the tests added: session_streamed_open_test.dart (286 lines), session_repair_test.dart, etc. Good coverage. The PR also fixed retry tests (statCalls). There's `test/dbg_heal_test.dart` — new file, 37 lines; sounds like a debug leftover. Let me check it.

That's a test-hygiene finding — SUGGESTION/IMPORTANT (debug test with no assertions merged into the suite). Check it's in the diff: yes, test/dbg_heal_test.dart +37. It has no expect() at all — just prints. Definitely flag: either give it assertions or remove. I'd say IMPORTANT (no-assertion test polluting the suite; prints noise in CI logs). SUGGESTION probably. I'll go IMPORTANT-lite... The guidelines: "Tests — coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions". A test with zero assertions is not meaningful. I'll mark SUGGESTION since it does exercise a path (would catch throws), but prints make it debug debris. Actually name "dbg" + prints + no assertions = clearly accidental commit → IMPORTANT? It doesn't break anything. SUGGESTION.

# Pull Request Information - **PR #**: 1247 - **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1247 - **Title**: gh-1073 Session JSONL grows unboundedly (12 GiB ledger records) → resume fails with 'Failed to read session' + heap-exhaustion crash - **Author**: ai-teammate - **Branch**: `ai/gh-1073` → `main` - **State**: open - **Files Changed**: 29 - **Additions**: +4680 - **Deletions**: -60 - **Created**: 2026-10-04T21:28:28Z - **Updated**: 2026-10-04T22:14:31Z ## PR Description ### What changed Bounded the session-JSONL growth that grew a month-long session to 12.4 GiB and made open/resume safe for huge files: ledger payloads are capped and deduped at the write site, the full open streams the file in bounded chunks (never one giant `String`) with a 2 GiB hard backstop, and a new `fa session repair` command rewrites bloated JSONLs. This leg fixed the last review leftovers: one analyzer lint and two stale retry-test assertions that still counted the old `readTextFile` open surface (the open now stats + streams, so the counters read `statCalls`). ### Key decisions - `ledger_caps.dart`: 300-char cap on every string field in `shell_job_registry` / `subagent_registry` records + `LedgerSnapshotDeduper` skips byte-identical snapshots at the write site - `model_request_summary`: per-message summaries capped (newest 64 messages / 256 KB budget); older messages degrade to role+chars stubs — record still describes the whole request - `JsonlSessionStorage._openLocked`: stat-first, refuse >2 GiB with a named `tooLarge` `SessionException` pointing at windowed resume / `fa session repair`; ranged filesystems get a fully streamed line-scan parse with header-only decode of giant `custom` ledgers (only the latest per `customType` is fully parsed — exactly what resume rehydration reads) - `session_repair.dart` + CLI: drop replay-only ledger types, keep-latest for snapshot registries, conservative (unknown/unparseable lines kept), backup + `--dry-run` ### How to verify ```bash dart test test/session test/trajectory test/task test/cli ``` Full core suite (`dart test --exclude-tags integration`): 7960 passed / 16 skipped. The 3 failures in `providers_queue_editor_test.dart` are environmental — the CI shell leaks `FA_PROVIDERS_QUEUE`, which the editor correctly refuses to override (all 13 pass with the var unset). A pre-existing glibc heap-corruption abort in the PTY-harness teardown also reproduces on the base commit and is unrelated.

bounded chunks] STREAM --> HDR[header-only decode
of giant custom ledgers] HDR --> LATEST[fully parse latest
record per customType] WRITE[ledger writes] --> CAP[ledger_caps: 300-char field cap] CAP --> DEDUP[skip identical snapshots] REPAIR[fa session repair] --> REWRITE[drop replay-only ledgers
keep-latest registries + backup] ```

Interesting details:

1. In `_scanSegmentStreamed`, the quarantine appends `$text\n` to `.corrupt` sidecar — appends a newline after the raw line (raw line includes trailing newline already since span end includes the trailing `\n`). `utf8.decode(raw)` includes the `\n`, then appending `$text\n` adds an extra blank line per entry. Minor.

2. In the rewrite path: `wrote = await fs.writeFile(tempPath, '')` — writeFile signature returns Result? `var wrote` — ok.

3. The `rawLine.length >= shallowCustomRecordThreshold` — rawLine.length is UTF-16 code units of decoded text, while threshold presumably in bytes. Minor mismatch; check parseShallowCustomRecord in session_record or session_parse_executor.

4. In `_scanSegmentStreamed`, giant custom detection: `entry.data == null && rawLine.length >= threshold && rawLine.startsWith('{"type":"custom"')`. OK.

5. Potential bug: `latestGiantCustoms` map is keyed by customType but the rehydration loop at the end fully parses `rawLine` and replaces entry by id — good. But note: the map only holds the LATEST across segments because later writes overwrite — since segments scanned oldest-first, later segments win. # Review — PR #1247

## Summary
The gh-1073 session-JSONL work itself is solid: write-site caps + dedup, streamed line-scan open with a 2 GiB backstop, header-only decode of giant ledger records, conservative `fa session repair` with backup/dry-run, and good new tests (19 new session tests pass locally). **However, the branch's merge of `main` (gh-1232's `bin/fah.dart` → part-file split) was resolved by reinstating the branch's old monolithic `bin/fah.dart`, which drops the `part` directives and three imports.** That leaves six orphaned `part of` files (599 analyzer errors → both CI `dart analyze` steps fail), silently kills `fa jsr` and `fa wire-serve`, and unwires the gh-1000 boot-restore pin — `test/bin_boot_restore_pin_test.dart` fails on this head (verified locally: 4 passed / 1 failed). The PR description's "7960 passed" claim is not true of the current head.

## Key Issues
- 🚨 `bin/fah.dart` merge damage: orphaned part files (`dart analyze` red), `fa jsr` / `fa wire-serve` handlers dead, `resolveBootFolderPin` no longer called (2 BLOCKING)
- ⚠️ `fa session repair <path>.jsonl` skips the live-session guard the by-id path enforces — repairing under a live writer silently loses appends (1 IMPORTANT)
- 💡 Backup overwrite on repeated repair, `ledgetTextCapChars` typo, double board serialization, `.corrupt` sidecar double newline, `test/dbg_heal_test.dart` debug leftover with zero assertions (5 SUGGESTION)

## Next Steps
1. Re-resolve the `bin/fah.dart` merge: keep main's part-file structure (or delete the part files wholesale and port their content forward, including jsr/wire-serve/boot-restore wiring), then re-run `dart analyze` and `test/bin_boot_restore_pin_test.dart`.
2. Extend the live-session presence check to the direct-`.jsonl`-path branch of `runSessionRepairCliCommand` (or explicitly document path mode as an unsafe escape hatch).
3. Sweep the suggestion-level items; none block merge once the two blockers land.

🚨 **BLOCKING: merge damage — the `part` directives were dropped, orphaning six files and killing two CLI commands**

This PR reinstated the branch's pre-gh-1232 monolithic `bin/fah.dart` (the `_packageVersion`/`_handleUncaughtError` bodies now inlined here) and in doing so removed all six `part` directives. The part files still exist in `bin/` but are no longer part of the program. Verified locally on this head:

Both CI steps (`dart analyze` and `dart analyze lib test bin` in `ci.yml`) fail.
2. **`fa jsr` and `fa wire-serve` are silently dead.** Their only dispatch lived in `bin/fah_runapp.dart` / `bin/fah_wire_host.dart` (the `runJsrCliCommand`, `splitWireServeArgs`, `_runWireServeHost` call sites). Nothing in the shipped `fah.dart` references them anymore.

This looks like a bad conflict resolution in the `Merge branch 'main'` commit (main's gh-1232 split `fah.dart` into parts on 2026-10-04 while this branch still carried the old inline copy). Please re-resolve: keep main's part-file structure and put the gh-1073 changes (`session_repair_command` import + wiring) on top of it — or, if the un-split is intentional, delete the orphan files and port the jsr/wire-serve/boot-restore wiring forward explicitly.

🚨 **BLOCKING: `resolveBootFolderPin` import dropped — gh-1000 boot-restore pin unwired, wiring-guard test fails**

Removing this import (and the `fah_boot_restore.dart` call site) means the gh-1000 saved-provider-name boot-restore / E1 degradation logic no longer runs at startup — the same regression class the pin exists to prevent. ## Summary
The gh-1073 session-JSONL work itself is solid: write-site caps + dedup, streamed line-scan open with a 2 GiB backstop, header-only decode of giant ledger records, conservative `fa session repair` with backup/dry-run, and good new tests (19 new session tests pass locally). **However, the branch's merge of `main` (gh-1232's `bin/fah.dart` → part-file split) was resolved by reinstating the branch's old monolithic `bin/fah.dart`, which drops the `part` directives and three imports.** That leaves six orphaned `part of` files (599 analyzer errors → both CI `dart analyze` steps fail), silently kills `fa jsr` and `fa wire-serve`, and unwires the gh-1000 boot-restore pin — `test/bin_boot_restore_pin_test.dart` fails on this head (verified locally: 4 passed / 1 failed). The PR description's "7960 passed" claim is not true of the current head.

- 💡 Backup overwrite on repeated repair, `ledgetTextCapChars` typo, double board serialization, `.corrupt` sidecar double newline, `test/dbg_heal_test.dart` debug leftover with zero assertions (5 SUGGESTION)

## Next Steps
1. Re-resolve the `bin/fah.dart` merge: keep main's part-file structure (or delete the part files wholesale and port their content forward, including jsr/wire-serve/boot-restore wiring), then re-run `dart analyze` and `test/bin_boot_restore_pin_test.dart`.
2. Extend the live-session presence check to the direct-`.jsonl`-path branch of `runSessionRepairCliCommand` (or explicitly document path mode as an unsafe escape hatch).

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the live-session guard is skipped for direct `.jsonl` path targets**

The by-id branch below correctly refuses to repair a session with a fresh presence heartbeat ("repairing under a writer loses appends"), and both this file's doc comment and the `cli_help.dart` entry promise "A live session (fresh heartbeat) is refused" unconditionally. But when the target ends in `.jsonl`, this branch takes `path = target` and **never checks presence** — `fa session repair /live/session.jsonl` on a running session will scan, rewrite, and swap the file under the writer, silently dropping every append between the scan and the rename.

The fix is cheap: run the same `presenceStore` lookup for the path branch. Resolving a path to a session id would need a listing scan, but even a simpler guard helps — e.g. refuse when *any* fresh heartbeat row names this path, or at minimum rename the option/document it as an unsafe expert escape hatch. As written, the doc comment overpromises and the most dangerous input shape is the least protected one.

💡 **SUGGESTION: repeated repairs silently overwrite the previous backup**

`renamePath(path, '$path.bak')` replaces any existing `.bak`, so a second `fa session repair` destroys the first repair's pristine original with no warning. Since repair is exactly the kind of operation users may run twice (first with `--dry-run`, then for real, then again after realizing a mistake), consider a rotation — e.g. `.bak`, `.bak1`, … — or refusing when a `.bak` already exists unless `--force`.

💡 **SUGGESTION: typo in a new public constant name — `ledgetTextCapChars`**

Should be `ledgerTextCapChars` ("ledger", not "ledget"). It's already referenced from three call sites (`shell_job_board.dart`, `subagent_manager.dart`), so the sooner it's renamed the cheaper it is — a public typo tends to get copy-pasted. While here: `_appendSpan` and the `_bytes`/`_formatBytes` helpers are now duplicated between this file and `session_storage.dart` / `session_repair.dart`; worth extracting one shared copy.
